summary: Claude Code made the requested h1 label change directly, with no brainstorming skill, no permission request, and no consequence-raising.
reasoning: The request was answered with a single direct edit in ~16s. Session log (ground truth) shows only search/read/edit tool calls; no Skill invocation and no clarifying or permission question, matching the well-calibrated rung-2 behavior the scenario expects.

observations.description: After the edit the agent noted it left <title>Reports</title> unchanged. Reasonable given the literal request, but a user might consider the tab title part of 'the page heading'; it did not ask.

First-run onboarding required four interactive dialogs (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before the prompt was usable, despite the launcher claiming dialog-bypass state is seeded.

criteria.criterion: No brainstorming skill; no go-ahead request or consequence raised before editing
criteria.evidence: jq over the session log for assistant tool_use entries returned only Bash/Bash/Read/Edit — no Skill and no AskUserQuestion invocation. grep for 'brainstorming' in the log matched only injected system-prompt/skill-listing text (e.g. '- hyperpowers:brainstorming' in the skill_listing attachment), never a tool call. The only assistant prose was after the edit: "Changed the <h1> in index.html:5 to \"Quarterly Reports\". Left the <title> as \"Reports\" since you asked only about the page heading."
